 Judgment
Respondent Nos.3(a-d)

being the legal representatives of deceased respondent No.3 in M.V.C. No.
550/1995 on the file of the learned Civil Judge (Sr. Dn.) & AMACT, Haveri (hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal), have preferred this appeal being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award dated 27.01.2004, awarding compensation of Rs.53,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. and directing respondent no.3 to pay the same to the claimants.
They are also challenging the amended judgment and award dated 15.06.2007 passed in the said case.
Parties shall be referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.

2. The claimants have filed the claim petition in M.V.C. No. 550/1995 before the Tribunal against respondent Nos.1 to 4 contending that deceased Gouse Moideen is their son, he was working as a Coolie and earning Rs.750/- per month.

On 28.04.1990 he had gone for coolie work, i.e., loading and unloading of bricks, under respondent nos.1 to 3, they being the owners of the tactor-trailer bearing reg. no. MYK-2273 and NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 5020.
Respondent No.1 was driving the tractor and due to his rash and negligent driving, the deceased who was sitting on the bumper of the tractor fell down and came under the wheels.
As a result, he sustained grievous injuries and immediately shifted to PHC, Shiggaon, thereafter to KMC, Hubli.
He succumbed to the injuries on 29.04.1990.

It is contended that when the claimants were in grief, respondent nos.1 and 3 have taken LTI of claimant no.1 on some white papers by misrepresentation that it is required for treating their son and also for postmortem examination.

It is contended that respondent No.1 being the driver, respondent nos.2 and 3 being the owners and respondent no.4 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.3 lakhs and accordingly prayed for allowing the claim petition.
Respondent No.1 appeared before the Tribunal represented by his Advocate but has not filed any objections.

Respondent No.2 filed objection statement stating that on 28.04.1990, i.e., on the date of the alleged accident, respondent No.2 was not the owner of the tactor-trailer bearing reg. no. MYK-2273 and 5020.
It is stated that he had sold the same in favour of respondent No.3 under an agreement dated NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 13.11.1989, by receiving valuable consideration.
On 01.02.1990 all the relevant documents were signed, including transfer form and

thus on the date of alleged accident,

The said fact was communicated to the executing Court.
Under such circumstances, it could not have proceeded to execute the impugned judgment and award by bringing the immovable property for auction.
The Court has committed a grave mistake of holding auction of the agricultural land ignoring the fact that the award amount was already deposited before this Court.
At the most, the claimants could have filed an application for release of the amount which is in deposit.
Therefore, sale of the agricultural land belonging to the appellants in favour of respondent No. 6 is void and the same is liable to be set aside.
Appellants are to be placed in possession of the said property.
Appellants being illiterate rustic villagers could not defend the claim of the claimants.
The Court was also very casual in passing the orders while executing the impugned judgment and award.

11. Learned counsel contended that the award amount is only Rs.53,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
But the executing Court sold the entire extent of the agricultural land measuring 4.30 acres in R.S. No. 341/2A - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 of Shiggaon village for Rs.7,00,000/-.
No enquiry was held by the executing Court as required under Order XXI Rule 64 CPC.
Therefore, the attachment and sale of the agricultural land is bad in law.

He placed reliance on the decision of the Apex Court in Ambati Narasayya V. M. Subba Rao and Another1; Balakrishnan V. Malaiyandi Konar 2; S. Mariyappa (dead) by LRs and Others V. Siddappa and Another3 and also the decision of the Co-ordinate Bench of High Court of Allahabad in Abdul Hafeez Khan V. Civil Judge and Ors.4, in support of his contention that the executing Court has violated the procedure contemplated under Order XXI Rule 64 CPC and therefore the sale of the agricultural land is bad under law.
12. Learned counsel further submitted that due to illiteracy and ignorance of the appellants, the appeal was dismissed for default, vide order dated 31.10.2015 but the same was restored vide order dated 07.08.2017.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent no.6-claimant opposing the appeal submitted that the claimants filed the claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation for the death of their son in the road traffic accident.

Respondent No.1 is the son of respondent No.3; respondent No.1 appeared before the Tribunal represented by his Advocate but he never contested the matter,
respondent no.3 even after service of - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 notice remain unrepresented.

After considering the materials on record the Tribunal came to the conclusion that respondent No.3 was the owner of the tractor-trailer in question which caused the accident but the same was not insured with respondent no.4 and therefore it is held that respondent No.3 alone is liable to pay the compensation.
When the award amount was not satisfied the claimants were driven to file Execution petition No. 26/2004.
Notice issued to respondent No.3 was returned unserved as he is dead.

When the notice was issued to his children being the legal representatives, for the first time they raised objection during 2005 that the award passed by the Tribunal is against a dead person as their father had died on 16.08.1999.
14. Learned counsel submitted that respondent No.1 being the son of respondent No.3 was very much represented by his Advocate before the Tribunal, but he never reported the death of respondent No.3.
Under such circumstances, the appellants cannot take advantage of their own wrong.

15. Learned counsel further submitted that the executing Court taking note of the contentions taken by the legal - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 representatives of deceased respondent no.3 dismissed the Execution Petition No. 26/2004.

The claimants were forced to approach the Tribunal once again by filing necessary application to reopen the case, to bring the legal representatives of deceased respondent no.3 on record after setting aside the abatement and condoning the delay.
The Tribunal again issued notice and the appellants have appeared before the Court represented by their Advocate.
But they never filed any objection to any of the applications filed by the claimants.
After affording reasonable opportunity, the Tribunal allowed the applications impleading the legal representatives of respondent nos.3(a-d).
Once again a notice was issued to them regarding the applications filed for reopening the case and amending the impugned judgment and award but they never appeared before the Court again.

The claimants have led further evidence seeking amendment of the impugned judgment and award and accordingly the Court passed the order on 15.06.2007 amending the cause title and operative portion of the judgment and award, holding that respondent nos.3(a-d) are liable to pay the compensation.

REASONS 24.

The appellants being the legal representatives of deceased respondent No.3 before the Tribunal are challenging - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 the impugned judgment and award dated 27.01.2004 and the amended judgment and award dated 15.06.2007 by filing the appeal on 30.10.2011, with delay of more than 2744 days.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that admittedly respondent No.1 is his son and he was already on record and appeared before the Court represented by his Advocate.
26. As per order XXII Rule 2 CPC where one of the defendant dies and the cause of action survives against the other defendant/s on record, the proceedings before the Court will not abate.

When admittedly respondent No.1 before the Tribunal was on record representing the deceased respondent No.3, contention of the learned counsel for the appellants that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is against a dead person and it is void, cannot be accepted.

However, at a later point of time the Tribunal allowed the applications filed by the claimants and impleaded the legal representatives of respondent No.3 including respondent No.1.
27.

Even though the appellants are impugning the judgment and award dated 27.01.2004 and the amended judgment and award dated 15.06.2007 passed in M.V.C. No. 550/1995, strangely they never produced copy of the amended judgment and award dated 15.06.2007 before this Court.
It is pertinent to note that the appellants while filing the appeal filed I.A. No. 1/2011 under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking to condone the delay of 2744 days in preferring the appeal.
The very same Mujeed Gouse Sab who was respondent No.1 before the Tribunal has sworn the affidavit making grounds for condonation of delay.

Strangely he has never stated anything that he was respondent No.1 appeared before the Tribunal represented by his Advocate and he has not stated anything as to why he had not brought to the notice of the Tribunal about the death of his father,
during the pendency of the claim petition.

It is also pertinent to note that even though the appellants contend that the entire proceedings in the execution case is vitiated since present appeal is pending,
it is pertinent - 22 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 to note that the appeal was came to be filed only after third bid for auctioning the property was held by the executing Court.
By that time, the appellants as judgment debtors were contesting the execution case represented by their Advocate.
The objections raised by the appellants before the executing Court was rejected vide order dated 18.06.2009.
Even though objection was raised for attaching the property, the said objection was also rejected vide order dated 04.02.2010.
None of these orders were challenged by the appellants before this Court.
28. It is also pertinent to note that the Tribunal issued notices twice to the appellants before allowing the prayer for amending the impugned judgment and award.
It finally passed the order allowing the applications filed by the claimants seeking impleadment of appellants as respondent nos.3(a-d).
The said order was also not challenged.

Even when the amendment of the cause title and the operative portion of the judgment and award was permitted, the appellants who were contesting the matter before the Tribunal never challenged the same before this Court within a reasonable Sri.

sentences.text: Even after filing the appeal during 2011 after holding the auction sale of the property by - 23 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 the executing Court, they were not diligent in prosecuting the same but the appeal was came to be dismissed for default, i.e., for non-prosecution as the objections were not complied, on 31.10.2015.

It is only thereafter the executing Court proceeded to confirm the auction sale accepting the third bid of the auction purchaser, directing him to deposit the bid amount, and issued the sale certificate as per Order XXI Rule 94 CPC.

29. Order XXI Rule 94 CPC makes it clear that where the sale of immovable property has become absolute, the Court shall grant certificate specifying the property sold with other details declaring the person as purchaser and the date on which the sale became absolute.
30. Order XXI Rule 92 CPC refers to the date on which the sale becomes absolute.

When the judgment debtors have not opted to file application under Rule 89 or 90 or 91 or even though they opted to file such application and the same was came to be disallowed, the Court shall make an order confirming the sale and thereupon the sale becomes absolute.
Therefore, it is clear that by the time the sale certificate was - 24 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 issued on 16.03.2017 the sale become absolute and the same was never challenged by the appellants.
31. Admittedly at this stage respondent No.6 has already sold the property in question in favour of a third party.
Therefore, the third party's right is created over the property in question.
Moreover, the appellants have not challenged any of the proceedings before the executing Court till today.
Under such circumstances, this Court can not enlarge the scope of this appeal to ultimately consider the legality of the procedure adopted by the executing Court.
However, incidental reference to such procedures adopted by the executing Court can not be held to be void.

The contention of the learned counsel for the appellants that the executing Court has not followed the procedure of holding an enquiry as required under Order XXI Rule 64 CPC and therefore the proceedings is void, cannot be accepted.
Under such circumstances, none of the decisions relied on by the learned counsel for the appellants are applicable to the facts of the case.
32. As I have already noted, the appellants are challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 27.01.2004 and also - 25 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 dated 15.06.2007.
The Tribunal has assigned valid reasons for holding that it is respondent No.3 who was the owner of the tractor-trailer in question and therefore held that he is liable to pay compensation.

I do not find any reason to interfere with the said finding as Sri. Majeed S/O. Mahamad Gousab vs Sannallabax S/O Gousumiya ... on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198725647/
12 respondent No.3 himself filed the affidavit before the learned JMFC seeking release of the tractor-trailer to his interim custody declaring that he is the absolute owner of the same as on the date of the accident.

sentences.text:
Under such circumstances, the appellants cannot find fault with the Tribunal in saddling liability on respondent No.3.
33.

Since respondent No.1 was a party before the Tribunal who was represented by his Advocate and since he is one of the sons of deceased respondent No.3, the appellant cannot contend that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal was against a dead person.
One of the legal representative of deceased respondent No.3 was on record and therefore the objections raised by the respondents is not sustainable.

The order passed by the Tribunal for impleading the appellants as legal representatives of deceased respondent No.3 was also never challenged by them and no grounds are made out to challenge the impugned judgment and award - 26 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 passed either at the first instance or by amendment of the cause title and the operative portion of the judgment.

It is pertinent to note that even though the appellants restricted their claim only against the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the learned counsel for the appellant never raised any grounds to interfere with the same, but the entire arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant is to attack the procedure followed by the executing Court, which is not the subject matter in this appeal.
34.

From the discussions held above, the conduct of the appellants in general and of appellant no.2-Mujeed Gouse Sab in particular, disclose that they adopted delaying tactics at every stage, since from the year 1990, as initially the claim petition was filed in M.V.C. No. 1175/1990 which was later re- numbered as M.V.C. No. 550/1995.

Even though an application is filed before this Court seeking condonation of delay of over 2744 days in preferring the appeal, I do not find any bonafides on the part of the appellants for condoning the delay.

The appellants were sitting on the fence, observing the Court proceedings and they were selective in approaching this Court, challenging only the impugned judgment and award passed by - 27 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 the Tribunal, without bothering about the execution proceedings where the property in question was auctioned.

When the appellants have not made out any grounds for condonation of delay or for setting aside the impugned judgment and award or the amended judgment and award, I am of the opinion that they are not entitled for any relief.
The impugned judgment and award either original or amended, is not liable to be interfered with.

Hence, I answer both the above points in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER I.A. No. 1/2011 filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of delay of 2744 days in preferring the appeal, is dismissed.

During the pendency of the appeal the claimants again filed execution petition in E.P. No. 94/2007 and managed to auction the agricultural property belonging to the appellants which was purchased by respondent No. 6, knowing fully well about pendency of the appeal before this Court.
The Court has committed a grave mistake of holding auction of the agricultural land ignoring the fact that the award amount was already deposited before this Court.
At the most, the claimants could have filed an application for release of the amount which is in deposit.
Therefore, sale of the agricultural land belonging to the appellants in favour of respondent No. 6 is void and the same is liable to be set aside.
Appellants are to be placed in possession of the said property.
Appellants being illiterate rustic villagers could not defend the claim of the claimants.
On restoration of the appeal, possession relates back to the date of dismissal of the appeal and therefore the proceedings before the executing 1989 Supp (2) SCC 693 (2006) 3 SCC 49 (2005 10 SCC 235 AIR 2009 All 162 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7288 Court holding auction of the agricultural land is also vitiated and the same cannot be upheld.

But, however respondent No.6 managed to alienate the schedule property in favour of a third party under a registered sale deed which is also not valid under law.
It issued notice to the auction purchaser and pursuant to the same the auction purchaser deposited the bid amount as directed by the Court and the auction was accepted by the executing Court.
On deposit of the entire auction amount the sale certificate was issued in favour of respondent No. 6 on 23.02.2017.
